The resulting presence–proxy pairs are temporally aligned with visual and motion observations, with sensor coverage and feature validity recorded separately.

Figure 13:Agent infrastructure and execution flow.The coordinator dispatches tasks to workers. Within a worker, the example graph connects planning, action generation, execution, observation, and verification; feedback determines subsequent decisions. Nodes invoke models, memory, and skills through the tool runtime. The environment supplies observations, while the body executes actions through the physical integration. Shared inference services allow workers to reuse model resources. Safety monitoring affects both graph progression and action execution, and execution records feed the web portal and reports. Solid arrows show the indicated execution, data, or service interactions; dashed paths carry safety signals and telemetry. Platform photographs illustrate simulator and robot categories.

Figure 15:Successful online recovery cases in RoboCasa365 and RoboDojo.After verifying task-state mismatches during WAM execution, the agent intervenes directly in the live environment. In RoboCasa365, it regrasps a misplaced pan and transfers it onto the active burner (top). In the RoboDojo memory task, it identifies an incorrect arrangement of two T-shaped blocks, grasps both objects, swaps their positions, and releases them with the required headings (bottom). Both recoveries ultimately satisfy the corresponding official success conditions.
